designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: The joke lands right away. Four 'Turn around.' steps between 'Choose the spot' and 'Sigh.' is real dog-owner truth, and the deadpan serif instruction-sheet format sells it. The brush line weight stays consistent, holds up as one ink, and works on black and white tees alike. Steps 6 and 7 are lovely, and the tiny huff marks on 'Sigh.' are the payoff. What keeps it from a $50 top shelf is the middle of the sequence: at full size the turning poses read as muddled anatomy, not rotation. Step 2's front legs tangle. Step 4 has a stray antler-like stroke on the back where a hind leg or tail should be. Step 5 is an upside-down head with a tongue that takes a beat to decode. Step 3 is just a standing dog with a motion arc. From 3 m the grid also feels a little evenly spaced and stiff.
designs.fix: Redraw steps 2 to 5 as one clear, progressive rotation: the same dog seen from the top or side, nose chasing tail, tighter at each step. Use clean, readable anatomy, with no stray strokes and no ambiguous limbs, so the repetition reads as a winding-down spiral that leads into 'Lie down.'
